title: Workflow, or agent?
intro: The week-1 ladder: fixed workflows vs genuine agency. Sort each system by which it is.

buckets.label: Agent
buckets.hint: The model decides what happens next

cards.text: Prompt A always feeds prompt B, then the result is emailed
Three models draft in parallel; a judge model picks — same steps every run
Summarize → translate → format, in that order, always
A pipeline that retries a step exactly twice on failure, per your code
The model chooses whether to call the record-question tool or just answer
It loops — act, observe, act again — until it judges the goal met
Given a vague goal, it plans its own sequence of tool calls
It decides mid-run to push a notification because the visitor asked to connect

debrief: The dividing line is who owns control flow. In a workflow — even a sophisticated one like parallel-plus-judge — every step was decided by you, in code, before the run. In an agent, the model owns decisions at runtime: which tool, whether to loop, when to stop. That ownership is what buys adaptability and what costs you predictability — which is why the agent bucket is exactly where termination conditions and guardrails become mandatory.
